rationale: Knowing and intentional chop-shop operation; retains the VEH 250 definition rather than treating ordinary repair as criminal.
Automotive stolen property for resale, not personal use; retains knowledge, intent and the greater-than-$950 threshold.
Retail stolen property for resale, exchange or return; retains knowledge, nonpersonal use and valuation limits.
Four organized-retail-theft alternatives remain separate; the receiving alternative requires two other persons. The instruction is not a substitute for the statutory punishment or aggregation rules.
Willful failure and wrongful diversion of dedicated construction funds. The retained instruction identifies a causation split; this association does not resolve that split.
Willful vehicle tampering or part removal without consent; does not require inventing an intent to steal permanently.
Temporary unauthorized bicycle and vessel taking; does not substitute these choices for motor-vehicle taking.
False government identification created to facilitate forgery, not every false identification document.
Knowing possession or display of false government identification with intent to facilitate forgery.
Counterfeit official or corporate seals with intent to defraud; the single catalog choice also describes a distinct possession route.
Possession requires knowledge, willful concealment and intent to defraud. Mere possession does not suffice.
Knowing possession of a forged document with passage/use and fraud intent; separate from blank and completed instrument branches.
Blank or unfinished instruments with completion and fraud intent; not the completed-instrument branch.
Completed instruments with passage/use and fraud intent; retains the published valuation and penalty limits.
Making or possessing counterfeiting equipment with knowledge of its counterfeiting use; ordinary equipment possession is insufficient.
Fictitious or altered payment instruments with fraud intent; does not close the separate insufficient-funds offense.
Unauthorized acquisition or retention with fraudulent use/transfer intent; does not close subdivisions (a), (b) or (d).
Making counterfeit access cards with intent to defraud; the same catalog choice includes the separate use alternative.
Using or attempting to use counterfeit access cards with intent to defraud; linked separately from making.
Unauthorized false signatures on access cards or payment documents with intent to defraud.
